   561		if every $O(a)$ is a binary observable, then the $B^u$ are the effects of a
   562		POVM with outcomes in $\F_2^t$, the Fourier-square measurement. Finally,
   563		if $C_\rho(O) \ge 1 - \delta$, then
   564		\[
   565			1 - \delta \le \E_a \, \Re \Tr\Big(O(a) \,
   566			\Big(\sum_u \chi_u(a) \, B^u\Big) \, \rho\Big) .

   582		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}. The final inequality

   672		$\hat{P}_a \hat{P}_b = 0$ for $a \ne b$. Consequently
   673		$Q = \sum_{v \ne 0} \hat{P}_v$ absorbs each of its summands on either
   674		side, $Q \hat{P}_v = \hat{P}_v Q = \hat{P}_v$ for $v \ne 0$, whence $Q$ is
   675		itself a projection and $C^0 = \Id - Q$ is a projection orthogonal to
   676		every $\hat{P}_v$ with $v \ne 0$. Splitting off the zero outcome in
   677		$\sum_u C^u$ leaves $(\Id - Q) + Q = \Id$.

   679		For $u \ne 0$ the compression identity is the expectation-preservation
   680		identity supplied with the dilation of Lemma~\ref{lem:naimark-helper},

   682		spaces cancel, the enlarged space having dimension
   683		$(\lvert \F_2^t \rvert + 1)$ times that of $\hilb$. For $u = 0$,

   687		$\sum_u B^u = \Id$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-fourier-transform}.

   690		for $u \ne v$ and equals $C^u$ for $u = v$ leaves the diagonal terms
   691		$\sum_u \chi_u(a) \chi_u(b) \, C^u$, and

   693		Lemma~\ref{lem:boolean-characters}. Taking $a = 0$ in the definition of

   984	\section{Applying the classical low-degree test}
   985	\label{sec:apply-ldt}
   986	
   987	The combined point and line measurements of the previous two sections are next
   988	merged into a single measurement returning a pair of global polynomials that
   989	encode the $X$-basis and the $Z$-basis information simultaneously. This is
   990	done by encoding the pair as one polynomial in $2m+2$ variables and invoking
   991	the quantum soundness of the classical low individual degree test
   992	(Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}). The classical game, its question
   993	distribution, and the line-point distribution are defined at dimension $2m+2$
   994	only when $2m+2$ divides $q$ (Definition~\ref{def:ld-game}), a condition that
   995	admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ does not supply; the statements below are the
   996	source statements, without that condition, and their proofs are blocked at
   997	the instantiation step for admissible parameters with $m \ge 2$. The
   998	obstruction is recorded in Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility} and
   999	analyzed, together with candidate repairs, in
  1000	\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}.

  1012		$\mathrm{combine}_{f,g} \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,2m+2}(\F_q)$ is defined by
  1013		\[
  1014			\mathrm{combine}_{f,g}(x, z, \alpha, \beta)
  1015			= \alpha f(x) + \beta g(z)\,,
  1016			\qquad x \in \F_q^m,\ z \in \F_q^m,\ \alpha \in \F_q,\
  1017			\beta \in \F_q\,.

  1020		Let $\ell$ be a line in $\F_q^{2m+2}$ with intercept
  1021		$u = (u_X, u_Z, u_\alpha, u_\beta)$ and slope
  1022		$v = (v_X, v_Z, v_\alpha, v_\beta)$, and let $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ be
  1023		lines in $\F_q^m$ such that for every point

  1031			= (u_\alpha + t \cdot v_\alpha)\, f(u_X + t \cdot v_X)

  1288			def:line-point-dist, def:ith-restricted-line, def:line,
  1289			prop:line-equiv}
  1290		The distribution $D$ is described by a sampling procedure. First sample
  1291		$(\ell, u)$ from the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and write
  1292		$u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$, so that Property~1 holds by
  1293		construction; all auxiliary randomness introduced below is sampled
  1294		independently of $(\ell, u)$. We write $\chi$ for the index function of
  1295		Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} at dimension $m$, whose
  1296		classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ for $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ partition $\F_q$
  1297		into sets of equal size $q/m$, and $\chi_{2m+2}$ for the index function
  1298		at dimension $2m+2$. The function $\chi_{2m+2}$, and with it the
  1299		line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ from which $(\ell, u)$ is
  1300		drawn, is defined only when $2m+2$ divides $q$
  1301		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}); admissibility of
  1302		$(q,m,d)$ supplies only that $m$ divides $q$, and for admissible
  1303		parameters with $m \ge 2$ the required divisibility fails, so this
  1304		first step is an unresolved obligation of the source argument, recorded
  1305		in Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility} and analyzed in
  1306		\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; the construction below is
  1307		carried out for the parameters for which the distribution is defined.
  1308		By a
  1309		\emph{fresh diagonal direction pair} we mean a pair $(s', w')$ with
  1310		$s'$ uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $w' \in \F_q^m$ having coordinates
  1311		$1, \dots, \chi(s')-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates
  1312		uniformly random; this is exactly the law of the coordinate--direction
  1313		data of the diagonal component of the line-point distribution over
  1314		$\F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}).
  1315	
  1316		If $\ell$ is axis-parallel, $\ell = (v, e_j)$ with
  1317		$v = (v_X, v_Z, \alpha_0, \beta_0)$ and $j \in \{1, \dots, 2m+2\}$, set
  1318		$\ell_X = (v'_X, e_{i_X})$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, e_{i_Z})$ where: for
  1319		$1 \le j \le m$, $i_X = j$ and $i_Z$ is uniformly random in
  1320		$\{1,\dots,m\}$; for $m+1 \le j \le 2m$, $i_X$ is uniformly random and
  1321		$i_Z = j - m$; for $2m+1 \le j \le 2m+2$, both $i_X$ and $i_Z$ are
  1322		uniformly random; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are the canonical line
  1323		representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the chosen directions
  1324		(Definition~\ref{def:line-representative}), so that $v_X \in \ell_X$
  1325		and $v_Z \in \ell_Z$.
  1326	
  1327		If $\ell$ is diagonal, $\ell = (v, s, w)$, then by the construction of
  1328		the diagonal component of the line-point distribution
  1329		(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} instantiated at
  1330		dimension $2m+2$) the direction $w = (w_X, w_Z, \gamma, \delta)$ has
  1331		coordinates $1, \dots, j-1$ equal to $0$, where $j = \chi_{2m+2}(s)$,
  1332		and its remaining coordinates are uniformly random. These remaining
  1333		coordinates may also vanish, so $w$ need not have a nonzero coordinate
  1334		at index $j$ and may be the zero vector, in which case $\ell$ is a
  1335		singleton (Definition~\ref{def:line}).
  1336		% The source proof describes w as "a direction vector whose first
  1337		% nonzero coordinate is j = chi(s)"
  1338		% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, proof
  1339		% of lem:qld-sublines); the distribution delivers only the weaker
  1340		% property recorded here, which is the one the argument uses. The
  1341		% source also leaves the laws of s_X and s_Z unspecified ("chosen such
  1342		% that chi(s_X) = j"); the uniform choices below are needed for the
  1343		% exact marginals claimed in Property 2.
  1344		Sample $\ell_X = (v'_X, s_X, w'_X)$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, s_Z, w'_Z)$
  1345		where: for $1 \le j \le m$, $w'_X = w_X$ and $w'_Z = w_Z$, with $s_X$
  1346		uniformly random in the class $\chi^{-1}(j)$ and $s_Z$ uniformly
  1347		random in the class $\chi^{-1}(1)$; for $m+1 \le j \le 2m$, the pair
  1348		$(s_X, w'_X)$ is a fresh diagonal direction pair and $w'_Z = w_Z$,
  1349		with $s_Z$ uniformly random in the class $\chi^{-1}(j-m)$; for
  1350		$2m+1 \le j \le 2m+2$, both $(s_X, w'_X)$ and $(s_Z, w'_Z)$ are fresh
  1351		diagonal direction pairs, sampled independently; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are
  1352		the canonical representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the directions
  1353		$w'_X, w'_Z$.
  1354	
  1355		Property~3 is immediate from the procedure: when $\ell$ is
  1356		axis-parallel, both $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are constructed to be
  1357		axis-parallel. The containments in Property~2 hold for every point
  1358		$u^\dagger = (u^\dagger_X, u^\dagger_Z, \alpha^\dagger,
  1359		\beta^\dagger)$ of $\ell$: the block $u^\dagger_X$ differs from $v_X$
  1360		by a multiple of the direction of $\ell_X$ when that direction is
  1361		inherited from $\ell$ (namely $e_j$ for axis-parallel $\ell$ with
  1362		$1 \le j \le m$, and $w_X$ for diagonal $\ell$ with $1 \le j \le m$),
  1363		and equals $v_X$ in all other cases, since then the corresponding
  1364		block of the direction of $\ell$ vanishes; in either case
  1365		$u^\dagger_X \in \ell_X$ because $v_X \in \ell_X$, and symmetrically
  1366		$u^\dagger_Z \in \ell_Z$.
  1367	
  1368		For the distributional part of Property~2, observe first that
  1369		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is a function of $\ell$ and of the auxiliary
  1370		randomness alone: the directions used are either read off from the
  1371		direction data of $\ell$ or freshly sampled, and by
  1372		Proposition~\ref{prop:line-equiv} the canonical representatives
  1373		$v'_X, v'_Z$ do not depend on which base point of $\ell$ is used to
  1374		compute them. Under both components of the line-point distribution the
  1375		point $u$ is uniformly distributed on $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and, conditioned
  1376		on the line $\ell$, uniformly distributed on the points of $\ell$
  1377		(each of the $q$ values of the line parameter, or the single point
  1378		when the direction vanishes, being equally likely). Hence, conditioned
  1379		on $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the sampled point $u$ is uniformly
  1380		distributed on $\ell$, and it suffices to establish the claimed
  1381		mixture description for the tuple $(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$ produced by
  1382		the procedure itself.
  1383	
  1384		Condition on the component of the line-point distribution
  1385		(axis-parallel or diagonal) and on $j$; the mixture of Property~2 is
  1386		over these choices together with the fresh index choices, and the
  1387		blocks $u_X, u_Z$ of $u$ are independent and uniform on $\F_q^m$,
  1388		independent of all direction data. In the axis-parallel case with
  1389		$1 \le j \le m$, the pair $(\ell_X, u_X)$ consists of the uniformly
  1390		random point $u_X$ together with the canonical axis-parallel line
  1391		through it in direction $e_j$, so
  1392		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},j}$, while, conditioned
  1393		additionally on $i_Z$, the pair $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ consists of the
  1394		uniformly random point $u_Z$ together with the canonical line through
  1395		it in direction $e_{i_Z}$, so
  1396		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},i_Z}$; the two pairs are
  1397		functions of the disjoint independent data $u_X$ and $(u_Z, i_Z)$,
  1398		hence independent. In the diagonal case with $1 \le j \le m$, the
  1399		triple $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ has $u_X$ uniform, $w_X$ with coordinates
  1400		$1, \dots, j-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates uniform,
  1401		and $s_X$ uniform in $\chi^{-1}(j)$, which is exactly the law
  1402		generating $D_{\mathrm{DLine},j}$; hence
  1403		$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},j}$, and similarly
  1404		$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},1}$ since $w_Z$ is uniform and
  1405		$s_Z$ is uniform in $\chi^{-1}(1)$; the two pairs are functions of the
  1406		disjoint independent data $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ and $(u_Z, w_Z, s_Z)$,
  1407		hence independent. The remaining cases are analogous: each of
  1408		$(\ell_X, u_X)$ and $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ is either built from the inherited
  1409		direction block as above, or from a fresh axis index or fresh diagonal
  1410		direction pair, in which case it is distributed as the uniform mixture
  1411		over $i$ of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ for the corresponding type
  1412		$\mathrm{v}$; and the two pairs are always functions of disjoint
  1413		independent collections of the variables $u_X$, $u_Z$, the direction
  1414		blocks, and the fresh auxiliary choices, hence independent conditioned
  1415		on the component. Within each component this yields exactly the
  1416		description of Property~2: the pair $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is
  1417		product-distributed according to the line marginals of
  1418		$D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and $D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on
  1419		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, each of $u_X$ and $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed
  1420		on its line, because under each restricted distribution the point is
  1421		uniform on the line conditionally on the line. The equivalent product
  1422		formulations follow from the same conditional uniformity.
  1423	\end{proof}

  2231		There exists $g(x,y)=\poly(x,y)$ such that for every
  2232		$\eps,\rho\ge0$ and every $\mu\in[1/2,1]$,
  2233		\[
  2234			\min\left\{1,\,
  2235				\mu f\left(\rho,
  2236					\frac{8p(\eps)+c(\eps+\sqrt{\eps})}{\mu}\right)+\rho
  2237			\right\}
  2238			\le g(\eps,\rho).

/-- An expanded point effect is self-adjoint. -/
theorem pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    ((S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a)ᴴ = (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq

/-- An expanded point effect is idempotent. -/
theorem pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
    (a : PauliScalar P) :
    (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a =
      (S.pointMeasExp side W u).effect a :=
  (S.pointMeasExp_isProjective side W u a).isIdempotentElem.eq

/-- The sandwich `M^Z_b M^X_a M^Z_b` is `(M^X_a M^Z_b)ᴴ (M^X_a M^Z_b)`. -/
theorem sandwich_eq_conjTranspose_mul_self (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
    (side : PlayerSide) (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a b : PauliScalar P) :
    (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b =
      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b)ᴴ *
        ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b) := by
  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul, pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose,
    pointMeasExp_effect_conjTranspose, Matrix.mul_assoc _ _
      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a * (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b),
    ← Matrix.mul_assoc ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a)
      ((S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a), pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self,
    ← Matrix.mul_assoc]

/-- The sandwich effects resolve the identity. -/
theorem sum_sandwich_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
    (x z : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
    ∑ ab : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P,
        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 *
          (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect ab.1 *
          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect ab.2 = 1 := by
  rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type_right]
  calc ∑ b : PauliScalar P, ∑ a : PauliScalar P,
        (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b * (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a *
          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b
      = ∑ b : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b *
          (∑ a : PauliScalar P, (S.pointMeasExp side .X x).effect a) *
          (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).effect b := by
        refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
        rw [Finset.mul_sum, Finset.sum_mul]
    _ = 1 := by
        simp_rw [(S.pointMeasExp side .X x).sum_eq_one, mul_one,
          pointMeasExp_effect_mul_self]
        exact (S.pointMeasExp side .Z z).sum_eq_one

point measurements, with outcomes in `F_q × F_q`.  This is the POVM of the
first step of the proof of `lem:qld-4-10`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:731-736`,

227:% The source (references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:257-274) states this
228:% definition for pairs of POVMs but applies the relation to arbitrary operator families:
229:% to plain operators at 06:313-330, to sets of matrices at 06:364-380, and to products and
230:% commutators, compared against the zero family, at 06:409-445. The general form below,
231:% for arbitrary finite families of operators, is the one of the NEEXP source
232:% (references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex:385-391), from which the distance
233:% calculus is imported; the POVM case is singled out after the display.
234:\begin{definition}[State-dependent distance between operator families]\label{def:povm-distance}
235:	\uses{def:povm-conventions, def:state-distance}
236:	Let $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal A$ be finite sets and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mathcal X$. Let $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal H$ be a quantum state, and for all $x \in \mathcal X$ let $\{M^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal A}$ and $\{N^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal A}$ be two families of linear operators on $\mathcal H$. We say that \emph{$\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are $\delta$-close on state $\ket{\psi}$ and under distribution $\mu$} if
237:	\[
238:		\E_{x \sim \mu} \sum_a \lVert (M^x_a - N^x_a)\, \ket{\psi} \rVert^2 \le O(\delta)\,,
239:	\]
240:	and we write $M^x_a \approx_\delta N^x_a$ to denote this when the state $\ket{\psi}$ and the distribution $\mu$ are clear from context. This distance is referred to as the \emph{state-dependent} distance. The principal case is that in which $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are POVMs on $\mathcal H$, and we then speak of the state-dependent distance between the POVMs; but the relation is used for arbitrary operator families --- for instance for products of measurement operators, or for commutators compared against the identically zero family, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:commutation-analysis} below.
241:\end{definition}

`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline

`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The

expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has

the marker-bound review body for the head SHA; no match means the ledger is
clean, and the paired `local-review/summary` status must agree.  Anything else
must be resolved, outdated, or adjudicated by the operator under §12 (Round cap
and operator adjudication) — the operator is the adjudicating party; the owner
